groups.title: Core Web Vitals Theory
groups.question: Your JAMstack site scores poorly on Core Web Vitals and does not show rich results in search. Explain what the metrics measure, how you would reduce JavaScript, and how structured data helps.

followUps.LCP, CLS, and INP metrics and what affec: What do LCP, CLS and INP measure?
followUps.Code splitting and lazy loading to reduc: How do code splitting and lazy loading reduce the initial JavaScript?
followUps.SEO structured data with JSON-LD and sch: What does JSON-LD structured data do for search results?

evidence.text: Largest Contentful Paint measures how fast the main content appears.
Cumulative Layout Shift measures how much the page jumps around.
Interaction to Next Paint measures how quickly the page responds to input.
Code splitting breaks the bundle into smaller chunks.
Dynamic imports and React.lazy load code only when it is needed.
Less code up front makes the page load and respond faster.

notEnough: Only saying it makes the bundle smaller.

evidence.text: JSON-LD describes the page's content in a format search engines understand.
It uses schema.org types like Article or Product.
It can make the page eligible for rich results such as ratings or breadcrumbs.

groups.title: SEO Fundamentals
groups.question: Search engines are slow to find your new pages, and shared links show no image. Explain how sitemaps, robots.txt and social tags help.

followUps.Sitemaps and robots.txt for crawl budget: What do a sitemap and robots.txt each do?
followUps.Open Graph and Twitter Card meta tags fo: What controls the preview of a shared link?

evidence.text: A sitemap lists the URLs you want search engines to find.
robots.txt tells crawlers which paths they may visit.
robots.txt does not hide pages from people, so it is not a security control.
Open Graph tags set the title, description and image of link previews.
Twitter card tags control previews on that platform.
A properly sized preview image is required for a good-looking card.

groups.title: Image and Asset Optimisation
groups.question: Your homepage loads large JPEGs and a web font that leaves text invisible for a second. Explain how you would optimise images and fonts.

followUps.Image formats WebP and AVIF for smaller: Why use WebP or AVIF instead of JPEG?
followUps.Preloading critical fonts and eliminatin: How do you stop fonts from blocking or hiding text?

evidence.text: WebP and AVIF give smaller files than JPEG at similar quality.
Image components in frameworks can generate these formats automatically.
Older browsers can be served a fallback format.

notEnough: Only saying they are newer formats.

evidence.text: Web fonts can delay text rendering while they download.
font-display swap shows a fallback font until the web font is ready.
Preloading critical fonts makes them arrive sooner.

groups.title: Lighthouse and Performance Auditing
groups.question: Performance keeps getting worse with each release and nobody notices until users complain, and one page responds slowly to clicks. Explain how you would catch regressions and diagnose the slow page.

followUps.Running Lighthouse CI in GitHub Actions: How would Lighthouse CI stop performance from getting worse?
followUps.Chrome DevTools Performance panel for di: How would the Performance panel help find why clicks are slow?

evidence.text: Lighthouse CI runs audits on every pull request.
It fails the build if scores drop below set thresholds.
The thresholds and pages to test are kept in a config file in the repo.
It records what the main thread does over time.
Long tasks block the page from responding to input.
You can see which code caused each long task.

notEnough: Only saying you record a profile.
